desc:
You may append lowercase letters, of your choice, to the end of s. Return the minimum number of letters that must be appended so that the resulting string consists of some non-empty block repeated at least twice (u + u, u + u + u, ...).

Example: for s = "abaab" appending the single letter a gives "abaaba" = "aba" + "aba", so the answer is 1. If s is already such a repetition, e.g. "abab", the answer is 0. For s = "a" the answer is 1, giving "aa".
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: If the final string is u repeated, every character s[i] must equal s[i + |u|] whenever both exist. Which block lengths p make that true for the given s?
Such a block length p is a period of s; periods correspond to borders: p is a period exactly when s has a border of length n - p (and p = n is always a period).
For a period p < n you must reach the next multiple of p, costing (-n) mod p letters. The block u = s itself (p = n) costs n. Take the minimum over all periods, not only the shortest one.
editorial: The result has length L and is a block of length p repeated L / p ≥ 2 times. The first n characters are our s, so s must itself obey s[i] = s[i+p] for all valid i: that is, p is a period of s (when p ≥ n there is no constraint, but then L ≥ 2p ≥ 2n, which is never better than the choice p = n costing exactly n).

For a period p < n the smallest valid length is the next multiple of p at or after n, which is at least 2p because n > p; the cost is (p - n % p) % p. The appended letters are forced to continue the periodic pattern, so they always exist.

All periods are n - b for the borders b of s, which come from the chain pi[n-1], pi[pi[n-1]-1], .... The shortest period is not always the best choice (for example a longer period may divide n-adjacent lengths better), so evaluate every period and keep the minimum. Total O(n).
solution:
def minAppendsToRepeat(s):
    n = len(s)
    pi = [0] * n
    k = 0
    for i in range(1, n):
        while k and s[i] != s[k]:
            k = pi[k - 1]
        if s[i] == s[k]:
            k += 1
        pi[i] = k
    best = n
    b = pi[-1]
    while b:
        p = n - b
        best = min(best, (-n) % p)
        b = pi[b - 1]
    return best
